Position: Telecommunications Technical Officer
Type: Full-time
Employer: Online Star PTY LTD
Location: Canberra ACT
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business
Online Star PTY LTD is a dynamic Canberra-based provider of telecommunications services and solutions, alongside IT services, dedicated to optimising business performance and unlocking new revenue streams in the rapidly evolving communications sector. With a team of highly experienced professionals, we partner with major telecom operators and vendors to deliver customised solutions that help clients enter new markets, defend existing ones, secure networks, improve quality, and deploy infrastructure efficiently. Our core values centre on innovation, operational excellence, cost-effectiveness, and high-quality service delivery, fostering a collaborative and supportive workplace culture where technical expertise drives tangible business outcomes and subscriber satisfaction.
About the Position
The Telecommunications Technical Officer plays a critical role at Online Star PTY LTD in supporting the delivery of NBN fibre and telecommunications network projects. This position involves field-based technical support, testing coordination, quality oversight and technical guidance across active project sites. The role sits between the Project Engineers and the field technicians and is essential to ensuring that network works are delivered to the required technical standards, that faults are diagnosed and rectified efficiently, and that completed works meet client acceptance requirements.
Key Responsibilities
Reviewing job packs, network plans, asset records and scopes of work before field work begins and confirming the design intent against site conditions.
Attending project sites to assess ground conditions, identify service and access risks, and confirm the scoped works can be built to the client design and NBN requirements.
Providing technical direction to field technicians during fibre hauling, splicing, pit and pipe works, exchange patching and BNTD installation.
Coordinating and verifying fibre testing using OTDR and optical power meters, and validating results against applicable NBN and client acceptance requirements before handover to the delivery partner.
Diagnosing fibre, duct, patching and connection faults on site, tracing the cause and setting out the rectification steps required to keep the job on schedule.
Checking completed works against the plans, job packs and NBN specifications, and confirming they are ready for submission to the project manager or delivery partner.
Preparing and updating as-built records, test results, site reports, defect notes and completion packs.
Coordinating with project engineers, supervisors, delivery partners, subcontractors and customers on site access, progress, technical issues and completion sign-off.
Monitoring crews on site to confirm they follow the approved work method, the SWMS and the relevant technical standards.
Escalating complex design, structural or safety matters to the Project Engineers or management where higher-level approval is required.
Reviewing rejected or non-compliant work, identifying why it failed, and instructing field crews on the correct method to bring it back to standard.
Keeping records of materials, equipment, test outcomes, network locations and work status to support project tracking and partner reporting.
Monitoring the performance of completed fibre network segments, interpreting transmission and optical test results, and identifying where network performance requires correction or improvement.
Configuring and integrating telecommunications network equipment, including BNTDs and related network access equipment, and verifying correct operation after installation.
Ensuring compliance with Work Health and Safety obligations on all project sites.
Requirements
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in a relevant field.
Minimum 1 year of relevant experience.
Strong technical skills in telecommunications network testing, fault diagnosis, equipment configuration and integration, including practical experience with OTDR and optical power meters.
Excellent problem-solving abilities, attention to detail, and the capacity to maintain accurate documentation and logs.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills for liaising with internal teams, delivery partners, vendors and clients.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment with a focus on quality standards and operational efficiency.
How to Apply
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

As the Senior Project Manager, you will lead, manage and be accountable for the successful delivery of the Enterprise Digital Infrastructure Capital Asset Refresh Program.

 

 






 

About Digital Infrastructure Services Team

Digital Infrastructure Services provides the foundational technology platforms that keep Tasmania's public health system connected, secure and operational.

The team delivers and supports the Department's enterprise data centres, compute and storage platforms, virtualisation, data protection, network connectivity, Wi-Fi and core infrastructure services that underpin clinical, corporate and business systems across the State.

Working in a complex 24 7 healthcare environment, the team plays a critical role in maintaining service reliability, cyber resilience, asset lifecycle management, infrastructure modernisation and the delivery of technology that directly supports frontline care.

This is your opportunity to become part of a high-performing team delivering digital infrastructure services that support hospitals, health facilities, clinicians, staff and the Tasmanian community.

The Enterprise Digital Infrastructure Capital Asset Refresh Program is a strategic program responsible for the ongoing lifecycle management, replacement and modernisation of the Department's enterprise digital infrastructure.

The program delivers the coordinated refresh of critical technology including enterprise compute, storage, virtualisation, data protection, Microsoft infrastructure, power protection systems, data centre infrastructure and other foundational technology platforms that support the delivery of clinical and business services across Tasmania.

Through proactive lifecycle planning and investment, the program maintains technology currency, reduces operational and cyber security risk, improves service resilience, and ensures the Department's digital infrastructure continues to meet current and future service requirements.

The Role

As the Senior Project Manager, you will lead, manage and be accountable for the successful delivery of the Enterprise Digital Infrastructure Capital Asset Refresh Program.

Leading the planning, governance and delivery of the Enterprise Digital Infrastructure Capital Asset Refresh Program.

Building, leading and operating high-performing multidisciplinary project teams.

Managing program governance, scope, schedule, procurement, financial management, risks, dependencies and benefits realisation.

Coordinating the delivery of multiple concurrent infrastructure initiatives across a complex enterprise environment.

Providing authoritative advice and reporting to senior executives on program performance, delivery priorities and emerging risks.

Establishing strong partnerships with business stakeholders, technical teams, vendors and service providers.

Driving continuous improvement in program governance, project delivery and infrastructure lifecycle management.

Ensuring the Department's enterprise digital infrastructure continues to support the delivery of safe, reliable and resilient healthcare services across Tasmania.

You will need

Demonstrated experience leading the delivery of large, complex ICT or infrastructure programs and projects within a complex enterprise environment.

Proven ability to build, lead and operate high-performing multidisciplinary teams, fostering collaboration, accountability and a culture of continuous improvement.

Demonstrated success managing multiple concurrent projects, competing priorities and complex dependencies while delivering outcomes within agreed governance, timeframes and budget.

Strong program and project governance capability, including experience managing scope, procurement, commercial arrangements, financial management, risk, issues, reporting and benefits realisation.

Sound understanding of enterprise digital infrastructure technologies and the challenges associated with delivering technology lifecycle and infrastructure modernisation programs. A commitment to continuous improvement, customer service, teamwork and delivering high-quality outcomes within a complex and fast-paced operational environment.

The Department of Health Tasmania oversees various hospitals across the state, including the Royal Hobart Hospital, Launceston General Hospital, Northwest Regional Hospital, and Mersey Community Hospital, as well as district hospitals and ambulance services. Additionally, it provides community health, mental health, and primary healthcare services to the Tasmanian community through more than 300 sites.

"## Structural Engineer

## Position Overview

We are looking for a highly skilled and motivated Structural Engineer to join our team and contribute to the design, analysis, and delivery of a diverse range of construction and infrastructure projects. The ideal candidate will bring strong technical expertise, a commitment to structural integrity, and the ability to collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary teams. This role suits an experienced engineer who thrives in a dynamic environment and is passionate about delivering safe, innovative, and cost-effective structural solutions.

## Key Responsibilities

- Analyse structural systems for both static and dynamic loading conditions, ensuring all designs meet relevant Australian standards and codes of practice
- Determine appropriate construction methods, materials, and quality standards, and develop detailed specifications, drawings, and construction procedures to guide project delivery
- Design structures across a range of typologies to ensure they perform safely and do not collapse, deflect excessively, or behave in any undesirable manner under load
- Prepare and review engineering drawings, reports, and documentation in support of development approvals, construction certificates, and project handover
- Conduct site inspections and supervise construction activities to verify works are being carried out in accordance with approved designs and specifications
- Assess and evaluate the behaviour and durability of construction materials, recommending suitable options based on project requirements and site conditions
- Collaborate with architects, civil engineers, project managers, and other stakeholders to develop integrated structural solutions from concept through to completion
- Identify and manage structural risks throughout the project lifecycle, providing practical engineering solutions to resolve design and construction challenges
- Prepare and review structural calculations, geotechnical reports, and material testing data to inform and validate design decisions
- Contribute to the mentoring and technical development of graduate and junior engineers within the team
- Liaise with clients, contractors, and regulatory authorities to ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards

## Required Qualifications & Skills

- Bachelor's degree or higher in Structural Engineering, Civil Engineering, or a related discipline
- Registered or eligible for registration as a Professional Engineer in the relevant Australian state or territory
- Demonstrated experience in structural engineering design across commercial, residential, or infrastructure projects
- Proficiency in structural analysis and modelling software such as ETABS, SAP2000, SPACE GASS, Strand7, or similar
- Sound knowledge of Australian Standards and the National Construction Code (NCC)
- Strong ability to prepare, interpret, and review engineering drawings, specifications, and technical reports
- Excellent problem-solving skills with the ability to deliver practical and innovative structural solutions
- Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage confidently with clients, contractors, and multidisciplinary teams
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously
- Full working rights in Australia

## Preferred Qualifications

- Membership with Engineers Australia (MIEAust) or Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) status, or working towards chartership
- Experience with Building Information Modelling (BIM) platforms such as Revit Structure
- Familiarity with sustainable design principles and experience delivering projects with a focus on environmental performance
- Postgraduate qualifications or specialist training in structural or geotechnical engineering
- Experience working on mixed-use, high-rise, or large-scale infrastructure projects
- Exposure to project management frameworks and familiarity with construction contract administration

## Why Join Us?

- Work on a varied and challenging portfolio of projects spanning commercial, residential, and infrastructure sectors, with genuine opportunities to advance your career
- Flexible working arrangements available, including hybrid options, to support a healthy work-life balance
- Ongoing investment in your professional development, including support for CPEng chartership, training programmes, and industry memberships
- Be part of a collaborative, inclusive team culture that values innovation, technical excellence, and mutual respect
- Competitive remuneration package with annual salary reviews and access to performance-based incentives

## Job Details

- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Superannuation"
